data.content_ref: inline:The claim that the panel is more reliable because it eliminates the 'expert's blind spot' (SRC_004) integrates with the 'closed-world' vs 'open-world' distinction (SRC_005) to suggest that 'genuine reliability' is actually just the ability to correctly identify the world-type. This is refuted if an expert consistently outperforms a panel in a closed-world task due to higher execution speed reducing the window for external interference.
